item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep talks to tech journalists Casey Newton and Kevin Roose about their new show 'Machine Gods,' which is coming to NPR.

item.title: As campaign season gears up, AI-generated ads are everywhere
item.description: Data suggests many candidates are embracing AI this year to boost their image and portray their opponents unfavorably. But whether it will turn out voters remains unclear.

item.title: Steve Bannon shares why he think AI development needs to be slowed down
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Trump ally Steve Bannon about why he wants AI development to be reigned in.

item.title: What to make of warnings that AI may pose an existential threat to humanity
item.description: Over the past week, fears of AI wiping out humanity are surging. But could it happen? And if so, how?

item.title: As AI execs worry publicly, Bill Gates would like a word
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Bill Gates, the former Microsoft CEO turned philanthropist, about his contributions to AI equity initiatives -- and his criticisms of an AI-powered future world.

item.title: Circuit training: How China is teaching humanoid robots to do useful things
item.description: China has made developing and selling humanoid robots an economic priority, but getting robots to work requires hours of repetitive "training" done by people to create data about the physical world.

item.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI
item.description: The rare pairing of a progressive leader and a MAGA voice is a sign of how worries over rapidly advancing AI are upending political alliances. But their policy proposals are far apart.

item.description: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark discusses growing concerns about artificial intelligence, recent warning signs and what he says companies should do to reduce the risks.

item.title: A roundtable on the rapid acceleration of AI
item.description: AI companies this weekend pushed out a new message: They want to slow down. This comes after several companies disclosed AI-related security incidents and raised concerns about the technology's future risks.

item.title: AI industry leaders call for development to slow down after recent safety concerns
item.description: After a string of security-related incidents involving AI agents and a high-profile resignation, AI industry leaders appear poised to slow down the pace of development to make sure it stays safe.
